sections.title: Provider adapter contracts and shared ownership

items.requestedAction: Decide which technical modules remain internal and which broader page owns their explanation.
items.rationale: The requested maintainer classification is complete for the exact 40 framework module rows with priorityScore < 15 in the 203-module inventory. Each has a source-reviewed internal-versus-broader-guide decision, reason, real canonical owner/document/heading, owned non-data source, source maturity and explicit remaining gap. The article distinguishes implemented nFacade from zero-score gateway scaffolds, retains all seven existing sourceOwnership mappings, excludes sibling Kickoff environments from framework inventory and avoids duplicating capability guides. This pass closes the requested classification/ownership explanation only; it does not close the retained guide-depth, implementation, installed-runtime, provider or full business acceptance gaps, nor promote 179 mention-based rows to detailed semantic coverage.
sourceFindings: Audit score weights counted schema/service/controller/router/data/test signals and classify uses mentions/thresholds for triage; there is no facade signal in the score. Current audit-source-coverage.mjs bytes, including the parent's corrected nPublish sourceAreas, are bound below.

Discovery field policy, ranking, source registry and query builder are implemented shared helpers. Domain projections, provider admission and authorization remain with consumers; all four receive distinct reasons and residual limits.

Loyalty Program, Redemption, Reservation and RewardType are schema-defined business contracts, not internal-only retirement. Loyalty reward method preparation and provider owner-API execution are distinct, with ledger authority preserved.
Rules operators and property/outcome registries implement generic extension contracts, not consumer-specific property semantics or side-effect execution.

Waste API secured routes/facade are implemented contracts rather than proof of persisted submissions. Waste reward assessment persistence is distinct from settlement; recycling handoff intents are not transport, outbox delivery, certification or physical completion.
Waste Receipt, Movement and Compliance retain their three existing SCHEMA_DEFINED owner-reviewed-reference mappings and explicit custody/logistics/legal limits.

Communication verification implements transient and stored challenges, bound one-use proofs, revision/readback and consumed receipts, not identity/business authority. SMS is injected sandbox-only; SMTP has controlled test transport; local delivery is simulation.

Engagement's source implements a one-way communication bridge despite stale scaffold wording in its local AGENTS. The register records that mismatch and leaves guidance reconciliation and durable retry acceptance to its owner.

Ollama/OpenAI/Claude/Gemini have real adapters and retain their four existing owner-reviewed-reference mappings. Request/response and stream limitations remain explicit; mockProvider is only an in-process test double.

Payment method preparation is not gateway execution. Callback HMAC/freshness/replay helpers require production store qualification; Stripe is offline sandbox code. CyberSource, PayPal and Visa packages have no source adapters and remain reserved scaffolds.

nFacade contains a generation template plus concrete cache/validator facades; its score of zero is not absence of capability. nSetup is deliberately non-runtime governance. nexusCore contributes inert initialization/acceptance descriptors rather than importing/publishing content itself.

All 40 table decisions link existing owner-qualified canonical heading anchors. Their residual guide-depth/implementation gaps are not silently certified by classification closure; sibling customer deployment guidance is described separately and not counted.
